questions.q: What is the relationship between AI Builder prompts and Azure OpenAI Service?
options: They are entirely unrelated products from different vendors
AI Builder prompts are powered by Azure OpenAI Service underneath — prompt builder is a wrapper around it
Azure OpenAI Service is a feature inside AI Builder's interface only
Azure OpenAI only works with Power Apps, never with prompts
questions.explain: AI Builder prompts run on GPT model versions powered by Azure OpenAI Service — prompt builder is the simplified layer on top of that underlying resource.

questions.q: What does a direct call to Azure OpenAI from a flow actually look like, mechanically?
options: A special AI-only action unrelated to anything from Chapter 1
A plain HTTP action making a POST request to the chat completions endpoint, with the reply parsed using Parse JSON
It requires installing a separate desktop application
It can only be done from Power Apps, never Power Automate
questions.explain: A direct Azure OpenAI call reuses the same HTTP action and Parse JSON pattern from Chapter 1 — nothing structurally different from calling any other REST API.

questions.q: Where does the generated reply live in an Azure OpenAI chat completions JSON response?
options: At the top level, in a field called 'reply'
Nested inside choices[0].message.content
It isn't returned as JSON at all
In a separate webhook callback
questions.explain: The chat completions endpoint nests the generated text inside the first choice's message content — choices[0].message.content — which Parse JSON can then extract.

questions.q: How can you create a brand-new AI Builder prompt without leaving the flow designer?
options: It's impossible — you must always switch to a separate AI Builder app
By selecting Run a prompt, then choosing New custom prompt from the dropdown, which opens prompt builder inline
By writing raw JSON into the trigger
By using the HTTP action exclusively
questions.explain: Selecting New custom prompt from the Run a prompt action's dropdown opens prompt builder directly, without requiring you to leave the flow designer.

questions.q: What is the purpose of placing a 'Start and wait for an approval of text' action after a prompt or HTTP call to a generative model?
options: To slow the flow down for no functional reason
To let a human review and potentially edit the AI-generated output before the flow acts on it
It's required by Azure OpenAI's API and cannot be skipped technically
To automatically reject all AI-generated content
questions.explain: Human review places a person between AI-generated output and whatever action depends on it, especially important for customer-facing or financial content.
